introduction_markdown: This paper is arranged in two sections, A and B. Answer ALL questions in Sections A and B. Section A: answer ALL the questions (15 questions); the mark allocation for each question is indicated. Section B: answer ALL four questions; all questions in Section B carry equal marks (15 marks each). You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Duration: two and a half hours.
enonce_intro_markdown:
![fig-1](gce-ol-maths-2021-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_B3_fig_1.png)

(i) Figure 1 is a Venn diagram showing 50 students in a boarding school who ate Rice ($R$) and Garri ($G$) for lunch on a particular day. All the students ate either Rice or Garri or both.

(ii) Using ruler, pencil and a pair of compasses only:

figures.legende: Figure 1: Venn diagram of Rice (R) and Garri (G) within S; only R: 17, R and G: 10, only G: x; no region outside the circles is occupied.

incertitudes: Q B3 : valeurs du diagramme de Venn lues sans ambiguïté (17, 10, x).

Q B3 (ii) : sujet sans barème par sous-question (15 points pour la question entière) ; les parties (i)(a)-(e) et (ii)(a)-(e) sont numérotées a à j. Le rayon mesuré dépend du dessin de l'élève : la valeur calculée (2,35 cm) sert de référence.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(a) Find the number of students who ate Rice.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rice eaters are those in the circle $R$: those who ate Rice only (17) plus those who ate both (10).

$n(R) = 17 + 10 = 27$.

**27 students ate Rice.**

All 50 students ate Rice or Garri or both, so the three regions add up to 50:

$17 + 10 + x = 50 \Rightarrow x = 50 - 27 = 23$.

**$x=23$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(c) Describe in ordinary English the region with the value 17.
questions.corrige_markdown: It is the set of students who ate **Rice but not Garri** (Rice only): inside the circle $R$ but outside the circle $G$.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(d) In set notation, give the number of students who ate both Rice and Garri.
questions.corrige_markdown:
$n(R\cap G)=10$.

**10 students ate both Rice and Garri.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(e) In set notation, describe the region with no student.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Every student ate Rice or Garri, so nobody is outside both circles. The empty region is the part of the universal set $S$ outside $R$ and $G$:

$(R\cup G)'=R'\cap G'=\varnothing$, so $n\big((R\cup G)'\big)=0$.

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(a) Construct a triangle $PQR$ in which $PQ = 10$ cm, $QR = 9$ cm and $PR = 7$ cm.
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Draw $PQ = 10$ cm with a ruler.
2. With the compasses set to $9$ cm and centre $Q$, draw an arc above $PQ$.
3. With the compasses set to $7$ cm and centre $P$, draw an arc cutting the first arc. Call the intersection $R$.
4. Join $PR$ and $QR$ to complete triangle $PQR$.

(The construction is possible because $7+9>10$. The angles are $\angle PQR\approx 42.8^\circ$, $\angle QPR\approx 61.0^\circ$ and $\angle PRQ\approx 76.2^\circ$, useful to check the drawing with a protractor.)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) Construct the bisectors of angles $PQR$ and $PRQ$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Bisector of $\angle PQR$:** with centre $Q$ draw an arc cutting $QP$ at $X$ and $QR$ at $Y$. With the same radius, draw arcs from $X$ and from $Y$ that meet inside the angle at $Z$. Draw the line $QZ$ (extended into the triangle).

**Bisector of $\angle PRQ$:** with centre $R$ draw an arc cutting $RP$ at $U$ and $RQ$ at $V$. From $U$ and $V$, with equal radii, draw arcs that meet at $W$. Draw the line $RW$ into the triangle.

Leave all the construction arcs visible.

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(c) Mark the point $M$, where the bisectors meet.
questions.corrige_markdown: The two bisectors cross at a point inside the triangle: label it $M$. ($M$ is the incentre of the triangle, equally distant from the three sides.)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(d) Construct a circle with centre $M$ such that $PQ$, $QR$ and $PR$ are tangents to the circle.
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. From $M$ construct the perpendicular to $PQ$: with centre $M$ draw an arc cutting $PQ$ at two points, then from those two points draw equal arcs meeting below $PQ$; join that point to $M$. The line meets $PQ$ at the foot $F$.
2. Set the compasses to the length $MF$.
3. With centre $M$ and radius $MF$, draw the circle.

The circle touches $PQ$, $QR$ and $PR$ (it is the inscribed circle of the triangle).

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(e) Measure and write down the radius.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Measure $MF$ with the ruler: the radius is about **2.4 cm** (any value from $2.3$ to $2.4$ cm is acceptable).

Check by calculation: the semi-perimeter is $s=\dfrac{10+9+7}{2}=13$, the area is $\sqrt{13\times 3\times 4\times 6}=\sqrt{936}\approx 30.6\ \text{cm}^2$ (Heron's formula), and the radius of the inscribed circle is $r=\dfrac{\text{Area}}{s}=\dfrac{30.6}{13}\approx 2.35$ cm.
